race.comment: LUNA WILL DO (8) has the strongest case after resuming with a narrow second to Dawn Dancer in Open company at Belmont, beaten just under a length after travelling well and looming to win. That form was seen in the Max Simmonds on Saturday. Laid the foundations fresh and she can raise the bar now. FIREARM (1) is the obvious danger after charging home from the rear to win a Mdn at Northam, and his earlier second to OFFICIAL BUSINESS reads well despite the quick back-up and top weight. PUCKER UP (11) resumes off a Lark Hill trial placing and was last seen running second as favourite at Belmont, with her debut fourth to Dawn Dancer stronger than it looks after she began awkwardly and was held up. GREY OL' DAY (2) led and won a Northam Mdn as favourite, having already placed in Open grade at Belmont, and his current campaign gives him a genuine minor-winning hope. ANDALADY (6) was too good on debut and she can go on with the job.
